stories.title: Regulatory Capture by Anthropic Through METR
TIDE: Reclaiming Lost Performance In On-Policy Reinforcement Learning
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.17924v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Synchronous, colocated RL post-training of large language models (LLMs) today suffers from severe under-utilization due to long-tail rollouts. Inference engines fall idle waiting for long-tail rollouts or decode at low, inefficient batch sizes.

stories.title: Tracing Knowledge and Reasoning in LLM
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.17461v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Current evaluations of Large Language Models (LLMs) report performance at the dataset or task level, revealing what a model achieves but offering little insight into the internal processing associated with its performance. We propose a task-centric framework for characterising the model-internal processing elicited by a benchmark.

stories.title: RAG-FGO: Dynamic Optimization of Query-Rewriting Agents for Generative RAG
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.17788v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), query rewriting serves as a core interface that aligns user intent with external knowledge bases, and its effectiveness directly determines overall system performance. However, generative retrieval faces three critical challenges in real-world deployment: noisy retrieval feedback, the difficulty of jointly opt

stories.title: CarryOn: Learning What to Keep in Context for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.17808v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents can coordinate tools and applications to complete complex, multi-step tasks. As their interaction histories grow, effective context management becomes essential for reliable and efficient execution.

stories.title: VEPO: Mitigating Multilingual Hallucinations in LVLMs via Visual Evidence-guided Preference Optimization
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18096v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) achieve strong multimodal performance, yet they remain prone to object hallucination---generating answers that are linguistically fluent but visually ungrounded. stories.title: Check Token: Real-Time Self-Verification and Precise Truncation in LLM Reasoning
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18564v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: ECC memory embeds 8 parity bits for every 64 data bits and automatically detects and corrects errors on each read. The parity bits carry no data and only safeguard integrity, at ~12.5% overhead.

stories.title: Quantize, Qualify, Rerank: A Recipe for Compressing LLMs Without Losing Quality
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18587v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Compressing large language models lowers serving cost, but a single automatic metric may miss quality loss. For the WMT26 Model Compression constrained track, we compress google/gemma-3-12b-it (24.4 GB in bf16) for three translation directions on one H100.

stories.title: Skill-Latent Rewards: LLM-Guided Reward Formulation for Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18597v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-horizon reinforcement learning under sparse and delayed feedback remains an open challenge. Existing return-decomposition methods redistribute episodic rewards to ease credit assignment, but they operate on raw state--action transitions and disregard the subgoal structure that governs meaningful progress in complex tasks.

stories.title: Not All Data Leakage Is Equal: A Controlled Benchmark of Evaluation Inflation in Tabular Classification
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18598v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data leakage is widely recognized as a threat to trustworthy machine-learning evaluation, yet the phrase covers mechanisms with very different statistical consequences. stories.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Mambas Selective Gate in Financial Markets: A Leakage-Controlled Study
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18599v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Selectively gated state-space models (SSMs), notably Mamba, are increasingly used for financial time series, yet how they internally represent market regimes (bull, bear, sideways) remains opaque. stories.title: Multimodal Fusion with Pre-trained Models for Psychotherapy Outcome Prediction from Emotional Dynamics
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18635v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In-session emotional dynamics are associated with psychotherapy outcomes but difficult to measure at scale. Pretrained multimodal models provide automated access to facial, vocal, and textual signals, yet clinical datasets remain small.

stories.title: Predictive maintenance in manufacturing: The operational value of continual machine learning
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18636v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Predictive maintenance in high-volume manufacturing often faces a domain-incremental learning problem: as new product configurations enter production, prediction models must learn from newly available data while preserving performance on earlier configurations that remain in operation. In this paper, we empirically study the operational value of cont

stories.title: GRAFT: Cross-Backbone LoRA Reuse for Continual Language and Multimodal Learning
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18638v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In continual learning, parameter-efficient fine-tuning enables large language models to acquire new capabilities through lightweight adapters such as LoRA, yet the reuse of pretrained adapters is typically restricted to models sharing the same backbone. This limits the transfer of learned capabilities from language models to multimodal models.

stories.title: SynthDCB: World Distillation for Scalable Device Control Benchmarking
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18639v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scaling device-control evaluation requires scaling both the worlds agents interact with and the tasks they must solve. We introduce SynthDCB, a scalable benchmark for environment awareness and device control built through world distillation.

stories.title: SERAG: SEmantical and Relational approach for Anomaly detection on knowledge Graphs
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18640v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Knowledge graphs constructed from text can contain facts that are individually plausible yet inconsistent with their relational context. We introduce SERAG, a supervised anomaly detector that combines two complementary plausibility estimates: a semantic score computed from separately encoded subject, relation, and object labels, and a relational scor

stories.title: HIMX: mixed-format matrix multiplication based on customized HIFLOAT4 representations
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18641v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: 4-bit weight-activation quantization (W4A4) is an important approach for efficient large language model (LLM) inference. Recent hierarchical formats such as HiFloat4 (HIF4) improve the representational range of 4-bit quantization through multi-level scaling.

stories.title: FedFit: Federated Dynamic Sparse Training via Fisher Information scoring
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18643v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cross-device Federated Learning (FL) is frequently bottlenecked by the prohibitive memory and communication costs of training deep neural networks on resource-constrained edge hardware. While federated dynamic sparse training aims to alleviate these costs by adjusting sparse structures during training, existing methods rely on magnitude-based heurist

stories.title: Minari: Infrastructure for Collaborative Reinforcement Learning Datasets
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18644v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Offline reinforcement learning (RL) depends on shared datasets, but sharing them is still hard. Each benchmark ships its own format, documentation is thin, and most datasets cannot be regenerated once the environment code moves on.

stories.title: RSIMed: Scaling Medical Foundation Models beyond Limited Clinical Data via Retrieval-Grounded Self-Evolution
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18646v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rare diseases are hard to diagnose, and the labeled clinical records needed to train models for them are few, private, and slow to extend, since a specialist must read every case. A model that writes its own training tasks could learn beyond these records, but no program can check a model-written diagnosis, and a wrong answer key corrupts training.

stories.title: Screen Before You Add: Reducing Candidate Inference in Model Ensembles
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18647v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As new models become available, existing ensembles must be updated to be competitive, making them intrinsically dynamic. Deciding whether to add a candidate model can require inference on an entire annotated dataset.

stories.title: Rethinking Offline On-Policy Distillation: From Scalar Advantages to Distributional Supervision
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18648v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers teacher capabilities through token-level feedback on student-generated trajectories, but repeatedly evaluating fresh rollouts with the teacher is computationally expensive. Offline methods such as Lightning OPD reduce this cost by caching recorded tokens' teacher log-probabilities on fixed reference rollouts.

stories.title: Algebraic Interaction: A Recipe for Neural Architecture Generation
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18649v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce an algebraic foundation for neural architecture design in which convolution, attention, state-space models, and equivariant layers are expressed through compositions of bilinear product operators over two structures: a position algebra governing positional routing and a feature algebra governing feature interactions. This decomposition m

stories.title: MeltKV: Memory-Aligned KV Cache Compression via Variable-Bit Packed Vector Quantization for Long-Context LLMs
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18652v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly rely on long contexts, making Key-Value (KV) caches dominate memory usage and inference latency. Existing vector quantization (VQ) methods effectively compress KV caches to sub-4-bit levels but often overlook inefficiencies in memory alignment and decoding speed.

stories.title: Earth World Model: Physics-constrained latent dynamics for forecasting and environmental scenario analysis
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18654v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: World models have been widely applied to multi-agent planning and forecasting, but exogenous environmental changes are rarely incorporated as replaceable drivers in a unified state-evolution process. This limits assessment of whether environmental perturbations propagate through physical systems with faithful dynamics.

stories.title: Beveridge: Open Weight System One Decision Models with Calibrated Probabilities
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18655v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many production systems need a model to make a narrow decision about a document (route a ticket, check a limit, refuse a request, pick the next step of a browser agent) rather than to write text about it. stories.title: SART: Sign-Absolute Reformulation Theory for Binary Variable Reduction in Neural Network Verification
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18657v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Complete formal verification of neural networks is crucial for their deployment in safety-critical domains. A key bottleneck stems from encoding complexity: traditional methods assign one binary variable per unstable ReLU neuron.

stories.title: Rethinking the Verification of Machine Unlearning
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18658v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine unlearning claims require evidence that a model has removed the influence of specified training data. Yet widely deployable post hoc verifiers.

stories.title: Stagewise Adaptive Boosting
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18662v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stagewise algorithms and sparsity-inducing regularization are two influential approaches to high-dimensional modeling. stories.title: Can a Vision-Language Model Tune Clustering In Context?
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18768v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Clustering is a widely used unsupervised learning method, but selecting an appropriate algorithm and set of hyperparameters for a specific dataset can require many possible configurations and evaluations. stories.title: Gradient-Guided Hardware-Native MIXFP4
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18769v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Blackwell tensor cores support native inference with 4-bit weights and activations (W4A4), but NVFP4 leaves a perplexity (PPL) gap to BF16. Choosing a format for each 16-element block can improve accuracy, but current matrix multiply instructions cannot execute choices this fine.

stories.title: Setting Optimal Reserve Prices using Fine-Tuned Language Models
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18785v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Online auction houses must set reserve prices for highly differentiated products whose unstructured descriptions contain valuable demand information. Existing approaches generally require managers to specify product attributes in advance.

stories.title: Hybrid Compression for Memory-Efficient Matrix-Vector Multiplication
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18792v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Iterative machine-learning algorithms repeatedly access large real-valued matrices through matrix-vector products, and their performance is limited by memory bandwidth rather than arithmetic throughput. Lossless compression schemes that support computation directly over the compressed data reduce both the data moved and the memory footprint of these

stories.title: Actuarial-Informed Neural Networks: Constrained Deep Learning for Sex-Specific Multi-Population Longevity Forecasting
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18802v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce Actuarial-Informed Neural Networks (AINN), a constrained deep learning framework for sex-specific multi-population longevity forecasting that embeds actuarial knowledge into LSTM training through differentiable penalty terms. Applied to a high-longevity 6-country cluster (Switzerland, Sweden, Norway, West Germany, Netherlands, Japan; 195

stories.title: Clustering-Based Artificial Tree Ensembles for Random Forest Approximation
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18803v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Random Forests (RFs) offer strong prediction performance but are difficult to interpret. Most representative trees (MRTs) and artificial representative trees (ARTs) provide surrogate explanations, but a single tree may miss patterns within a forest.

stories.title: Recovered or Memorized? Investigating Dynamical Consistency and Faithfulness in World Model Latents
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18807v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: World models develop internal simulators that can learn the structure and dynamics of an environment. It has been demonstrated that their internal representations are both meaningful and causal, but are these representations faithful to the governing dynamics of the environment they are learning?

stories.title: LEAP-LLM: Preserving lead-time structure for question-conditioned ECG interpretation
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18809v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The electrocardiogram (ECG) records cardiac electrical activity across multiple leads and is used for detecting cardiac abnormalities. Recent ECG-language models enable large language models (LLMs) to interpret cardiac signals and answer clinically relevant questions.

stories.title: What to Practice Next? Latent Profile-Guided Task Selection for Skill-Evolving LLM Agents
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18818v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Task selection shapes the experiences available for skill evolution in LLM agents, yet fixed practice schedules overlook differences in skill requirements and evolving task value. Most existing methods, however, rely on fixed schedules or scalar measures of progress, leaving nonstationary skill demands unaddressed.

stories.title: Identification and external validation of the sets of 4-, 6-, 8-, 12-, and 24-hour CGM motifs
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18844v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: There is growing interest in using CGM for purposes other than those initially intended. Recent work of Lobo et al.

stories.title: Self-Improvement Memory Enables Continual Recursive Self-Improvement
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18856v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Harness optimization is often studied with a fixed policy model and benchmark. When either changes, the optimizer must decide which parts of an evolved harness to reuse or revise, but the harness alone may not explain why earlier edits were made or how they performed.

stories.title: SLICES: A Benchmark and Evaluation Framework for Self-Supervised Learning on Sparse ICU Time Series
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18868v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Self-supervised learning (SSL) results for intensive care unit (ICU) time series are hard to compare when data processing, encoders, and adaptation vary together. We present SLICES, a benchmark and evaluation framework for comparing and extending SSL methods under a shared clinical setup.

stories.title: Factorized Self-Supervised Speech Tokenization
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18898v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Speech tokenizers convert audio into discrete units, enabling language models to process and generate speech. The goal is to learn compact, text-like representations while preserving enough detail to reconstruct a speaker's voice and delivery.

stories.title: How Much Do Foundation Models Add to Gradient Boosting on Financial Event Sequences?
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18914v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Foundation models pretrained on raw transaction sequences are proposed for credit, fraud and churn modeling, with reported gains over gradient boosting, but the data and baselines behind these gains are rarely public. We measure how much the pretraining and adaptation recipes of these models add to a baseline of point-in-time window aggregates and Li

stories.title: The Human Side of ML Engineering: Analyzing the Collaboration and Communication Skills in ML Job Postings
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18915v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Studies of Machine Learning (ML) practice highlight the importance of combining technical expertise with interpersonal capabilities, particularly collaboration and communication. However, evidence on how ML job postings express these skills is scarce, and prior work largely relies on keyword-based analyses that overlook implicit expression.

stories.title: Simplify, Agree, Distill: Label-Free Self-Distillation with Stepping Stones
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18916v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can a language model teach itself to reason without labels? On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) uses the model as its own teacher, but strengthens that teacher with a ground-truth solution.

stories.title: Human vs Machine Translation Detection: A Cross-Model, Cross-Domain, and Low-Resource Analysis
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18586v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The growing reliance on web-crawled corpora for training large language models introduces a critical challenge: machine-translated (MT) content is often treated as human translation (HT), potentially degrading data quality and propagating synthetic artifacts, especially in low-resource settings. In this work, we study MT-HT detectability across high-

stories.title: Automating literature screening and knowledge synthesis with large language models
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18588v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scientific literature is expanding rapidly, yet much of its knowledge remains difficult to organize and reuse due to the substantial workload needed to navigate large, heterogeneous literature corpora. Here, we develop a generalizable large language model (LLM)-powered framework that automates literature screening, structured information extraction,

stories.title: OmniTag-LLM: Multilingual Multitask Speech Tagging
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18589v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal LLMs promise to replace the traditional cascade of specialist speech models with a single system that, from one audio clip, jointly transcribes and labels emotion, gender, language, and named entities. Yet most benchmarks still score these tasks in isolation, and largely in English.

stories.title: Where Language Models Fail Like Aphasic Patients and Where They Don't
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18591v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The computational architecture of human word production -- whether semantic-lexical retrieval and phonological encoding constitute dissociable processing stages -- has been debated for decades using hand-designed models with small vocabularies. We introduce computational architectural dissociation: using known architectural properties of vision-langu

stories.title: Endogenous Preferences as Vulnerability Signals: Discovering Universal Adversarial Triggers for LLM Utility Degradation
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18592v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deployed large language models must remain useful when untrusted text enters their prompt context. Adversarial prompting and red-teaming methods typically define the failures they seek through task labels, harmful targets, judge feedback, or downstream utility scores.

stories.title: Theoretical Foundations of Computational Islamic Jurisprudence (Fiqh)
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18593v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents the theoretical foundations and a comprehensive formal system for Computational Islamic Jurisprudence (Fiqh). We begin by establishing six foundational principles that distinguish computational Fiqh from conventional natural language processing and general theological formalization.

stories.title: Whose Side Are You On? Measuring Stance at Scale for Reddit Discourse Analysis During the Israel-Gaza War
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18594v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large-scale discourse analysis often requires stance labels, yet for many high-salience political events such labels are unavailable at the comment level. We introduce and validate a comment-level stance measurement instrument that assigns Pro-Israel, Pro-Palestinian, or Undefined stance using Reddit comment text.

stories.title: Profiling Hallucinations in Frontier LLMs for Entity Linking to Medical Ontologies
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18595v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into healthcare promises to revolutionize clinical documentation and interoperability, yet reliability remains a concern. This study presents a comprehensive analysis of hallucinations by frontier LLMs tasked with mapping clinical text to SNOMED CT.

stories.title: Between the Lines: Multi-turn Contextual Investment Advice Detection
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18596v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As large language models (LLMs) increasingly power financial conversational assistants, detecting investment advice in natural language has become a critical regulatory and safety challenge. stories.title: ScopeBench: Evaluating Cultural Norm Scope Awareness in LLMs
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18600v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Safety evaluation in large language models treats harm as culturally invariant, yet a model cannot correctly apply a safety norm without knowing whose norms bind. We introduce ScopeBench, a benchmark that treats cultural scope as a first-class safety dimension.

stories.title: Jailbreak LLMs with Linguistic Style as a Hidden Attack Surface
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18601v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that linguistic style is a systematic and previously overlooked attack surface for LLM safety. stories.title: Internal Verdicts Track Evidence: A Template-Controlled Neutrosophic Reading of Epistemic States in Large Language Models via the Jacobian Lens
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18602v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For twenty-five years, neutrosophic logic has assigned independent degrees of truth (T), indeterminacy (I), and falsity (F) to epistemic states that classical and fuzzy semantics cannot express. Previous applications measured these components on outputs: answers, judgments, expert evaluations.

stories.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Clinical Decision Support in Gait Analysis: A Proof-of-Concept
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18603v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) demonstrate significant potential for clinical decision support but lack specialized biomechanical knowledge required for accurate gait analysis interpretation. stories.title: One Question, Four Voices: How Advice for Alzheimer's Caregiving Differs Between Caregivers, Clinicians, and Large Language Models
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18604v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Online caregiver forums are an important source of emotional and informational support for Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (ADRD). We compare responses to 85 real caregiver questions from ALZConnected across four responder groups: peer caregivers, physicians, ChatGPT, and a retrieval-augmented CareGPT grounded in peer discussions.

stories.title: Enhanced English-Sanskrit Translation using Multilingual NMT Approach
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18605v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural Machine Translation (NMT) is a widely accepted technique of automatic translation tasks of Natural Language Processing. However, NMT requires a sufficient amount of parallel corpora to attain a reasonable translation quality.

stories.title: Syntactic Complexity Convergence in Dialogue: Analysis of the Phenomenon and Application to LLM Detection
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18606v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We revisit the under-explored phenomenon of syntactic complexity convergence in dialogue. Extending prior topic-level analyses to full conversations, we examine five human-human datasets and a set of human-LLM dialogues.

stories.title: Justification of Emotional Appeal in Computational Argumentation
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18607v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Emotional appeals (EAs) are often treated as fallacious in computational argumentation, yet they may be justified when warranted by the context. We introduce the task of predicting EA justification and present the first human-annotated dataset for this task, covering 1,176 argument--context pairs.

stories.title: NYUAD at ArGuard Shared Tasks: Multimodal Embedding Models for Detecting Arabic Hateful Memes and Unsafe Prompts
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18608v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid growth of social media and generative AI has significantly increased the volume of Arabic textual content, memes, and user prompts shared across online platforms. While these media facilitate communication, creativity, and information exchange, they can also be exploited to disseminate hate speech, harmful content, and unsafe instructions.

stories.title: Many Paths to the Same Mistake: Generating Diverse Reasoning Paths Behind the Same Student Mistake
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18609v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Realistic evaluation of AI systems requires user simulators that capture not only cooperative behavior, but also the errors and variability that arise in real interactions. stories.title: Understanding Failures in LLM Reasoning by Learning Structured Representations of Chain-of-Thought
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18611v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) is central to improving reasoning in large language models, yet existing evaluation methods focus on step-level signals and ignore the underlying structure of reasoning traces. This raises a key question: what aspects of reasoning quality (i.e., correctness, efficiency, and failure patterns) are encoded in the structure of a Co

stories.title: When Helpful Agents Cause Financial Harm: Evaluating LLM Agent Safety in Executable Economic Worlds
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18612v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As LLM agents become increasingly capable of making consequential economic decisions, their safety under economic pressures remains poorly understood. We introduce EconSafeBench, the first benchmark for systematically evaluating the safety of LLM agents in executable economic environments.

stories.title: Bridging Semantics and Utilities: A Controllable and Scalable Market Simulation
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18613v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models(LLMs) have recently been used to construct generative agents for financial market simulation. Existing approaches typically prompt each agent separately with public market information and a private investor profile, and ask the model to directly generate trading actions.

stories.title: Self-Evolving Dual-Role Deliberation for Medication Recommendation from Clinical Records
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18615v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recommending medications from electronic health records (EHRs) is a safety-critical task that demands therapeutic coverage, explicit safety constraints, traceable justification, and continual adaptivity. stories.title: The Judge Is Not Impartial: Self-Preference in Medical LLM Evaluation
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18616v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to evaluate model-generated medical content, creating a potential circularity: an LLM judge may favor outputs generated by the same model independently of clinical quality. To characterize LLM judge self-preference in medical settings, we measured same-model affinity in single-turn specialist questio

stories.title: Assisting Patients with Reliable Information Gathering: A Guide to Building Efficient QA Systems for Medical Use
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18619v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The application of question-answering (QA) systems in the medical domain has rapidly advanced, significantly improving patients' access to reliable health-related information. stories.title: CondRelBench: A Mixed-Domain Benchmark for Condition-Scoped Relation Understanding
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18620v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Relation extraction systems often identify what a relation is, but not the condition under which it holds. This can collapse condition-bound claims into unsupported generalizations, a failure we call relation overgeneralization.

stories.title: Which Mathematical Context Supports Target-Aligned Conjecture Generation? A Paired Ablation Study
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generating mathematical conjectures from natural-language context is challenging because theorem-relevant information is distributed across multiple forms of mathematical context, including definitions, objects, assumptions, and constructions. stories.title: RGFC: Registry Grounded Function Calling with stage-decomposed evaluation
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18622v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-calling evaluations often report whether the final call matches a reference answer, but this single outcome merges different failures: choosing a function outside the available registry, violating the selected schema, or filling arguments with values not supported by the user request. stories.title: Skill Transfer: Adapting Agent Skills from Strong to Weak Agents
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18624v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent skills are modular bundles of instructions, code, and resources that an agent loads on demand, increasingly authored and validated on frontier models and shared as an open standard. stories.title: Interpretability-Guided Auditing for Clinical Language Models for Discharge Prediction
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18626v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Clinical natural language processing (NLP) models for hospital discharge prediction are vulnerable to explicit discharge-related lexical cues in clinical notes, even when note timestamps are temporally filtered. stories.title: EmoTrace: Recursive Trace-Factorized Generation for Emotional Support Conversation
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18628v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fundamental to effective emotional support is the iterative interpersonal dynamic wherein a supporter intervention continuously shapes the psychological trajectory of the seeker. While contemporary models capture variables at the turn level, including transient emotions and discrete strategies, they inherently treat these factors as isolated events.

stories.title: Decision 1.0: Towards Open Decision Foundation Models
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18629v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intelligent software needs reusable judgments inside its control flow: selecting an action, testing a condition, or assessing evidence against a rubric. We present Decision 1.0, an open-weight family that turns textual state and runtime-defined questions into typed probability distributions.

stories.title: All the Pieces Matter! A Six-stage Analysis of an Underground Fraud Ecosystem on Dread
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18630v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cyber-enabled fraud is a dominant global threat that causes severe financial loss, identity theft, and widespread psychological harm. stories.summary: arXiv:2611.17463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electric arc furnace (EAF) steelmaking plays an increasingly important role in recycled and lower-carbon steel production. stories.summary: arXiv:2611.17478v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Processing-in-memory (PIM) has been proposed as an alternative computing paradigm for training Deep Neural Networks, including Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). stories.title: Adversarially Batched Online Learning
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.17500v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce adversarially batched online learning, where the learner may update its decision rule only at a restricted set of time steps. stories.summary: arXiv:2611.17556v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Causal discovery promises to find which recorded variables drive a process target such as product quality, yield or energy use. stories.summary: arXiv:2611.17576v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Binary neural networks (BNNs) reduce model storage and replace many arithmetic operations with efficient bitwise computations, but the single-sign activation limits their representational capacity.
